New elements that came with it: **mihrab** (prayer niche), **minbar** (pulpit) and **minarets**.
⚠ **First true arch** = **Balban's tomb**; **first true dome** = **Alai Darwaza**.

37.s: In Indo-Islamic construction, what does 'surkhi' refer to?
o: Brick dust used in the mortar
37.x: Surkhi is brick dust mixed into the lime mortar in which rubble masonry was set.
xa: The **arcuate** style (arch, dome, vault) came with the **Turks**; the Indian **trabeate** style used lintel, pillar and corbel.
**Jali** = pierced stone screens; **arabesque** = floral vines.
Two broad styles: **Imperial** (Delhi Sultans) vs **Provincial** (regional dynasties).

37.s: In Indo-Islamic architecture, what is the 'mihrab'?
37.x: The mihrab is the prayer niche; the pulpit is the minbar and the jali is the pierced stone screen.
xa: **Arcuate** style (arch, dome, vault) was brought by the **Turks**; **true arch** held by a **keystone**.
**Trabeate** = Indian lintel, pillar, corbel style.
Rubble masonry used **lime mortar** with **surkhi** (brick dust).
Decoration avoided human/animal figures: **geometric** patterns, **arabesque**, **Quranic calligraphy**.

37.s: The decoration of the Indo-Islamic style moved away from which of the following?
37.x: Indo-Islamic decoration moved away from human and animal figures towards geometric patterns, arabesque and Quranic calligraphy.
xa: **Jali** (pierced stone screens) was the other key decorative device.
The **Qutb Minar** carries **Quranic calligraphy bands** on its tapering storeys.
Two broad styles: **Imperial** (Delhi Sultans) and **Provincial** (regional dynasties).

37.s: What are pierced stone screens in Indo-Islamic buildings called?
37.x: A jali is a pierced stone screen; the mihrab is the prayer niche and the minbar the pulpit.

37.s: In the arcuate style, what holds the true arch in place?
37.x: The true arch of the arcuate style is held by a keystone; lintel, pillar and corbel belong to the trabeate style.

37.s: On which of the following was the Indian trabeate style of building based?
37.x: Trabeate is the Indian lintel-pillar-corbel style; arch, dome and vault form the Turkish arcuate style.

37.s: The Horse-Shoe arch was first introduced in the -
37.x: The Horse-Shoe arch was first introduced in the Alai Darwaza. It was built by Alauddin Khalji.

37.s: The first true arch in the Sultanate memorial could be seen in
37.x: Tomb of Balban is located in Mehrauli, New Delhi. It was here that first true arches made their appearance in India.

37.s: In which year was Sultan Ghari, the first Indo-Islamic tomb in India, built?
37.x: Sultan Ghari dates to 1231, before Balban's tomb, Alai Darwaza and the octagonal tomb of Khan-i-Jahan Tilangani.
xa: ⚠ **Sultan Garhi – Balban's tomb – Alai Darwaza** = first **tomb – true arch – true dome**.
Sultan Ghari was the tomb of Iltutmish's son **Nasiruddin Mahmud**.
**Octagonal tombs** became a hallmark of the **Lodi** (and Sayyid) style.

37.s: Which building has the first true dome and was the first built fully on Islamic principles by Indian craftsmen?
37.x: Alai Darwaza is credited with the first true dome and with being the first building based fully on Islamic principles by Indian craftsmen.
37.tq: Distinguish the ‘first true dome’ from the separately tested first tomb and first true arch.
xs: The **first true dome** and first building on fully **Islamic principles** by Indian craftsmen = **Alai Darwaza** — option **(3)**.
Built by **Alauddin Khalji** in **1311** as the gateway of the **Quwwat-ul-Islam** mosque, Qutb complex.
**Sultan Ghari** is the first tomb; **Tughlaqabad** is Ghiyasuddin's fort-city; **Atala Masjid** is the Sharqi mosque of Jaunpur.
xa: Khalji hallmark: **horse-shoe arch with lotus-bud (spearhead) fringe**, red sandstone and marble inlay.
⚠ First tomb = **Sultan Garhi**; first true arch = **Balban's tomb**.
Alai Darwaza is part of the **UNESCO** site "Qutb Minar and its Monuments" (inscribed **1993**).

37.s: By what name is Sher Shah Suri's Sadak-e-Azam, one of Asia's oldest major roads, better known?
37.x: The Grand Trunk Road, called Sadak-e-Azam under Sher Shah Suri, is one of Asia's oldest major roads.
n: The Grand Trunk Road is one of Asia's oldest major roads. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 100-101]
The Grand Trunk Road is also known as Sadak-e-Azam. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 100-101]
xa: **Lingaraja Temple** = one of the oldest temples in **Bhubaneswar**.
**Gudimallam Shiva Linga** = the **earliest Shiva Linga**.
**Gupta period** = the **earliest freestanding temples**.

37.s: For which of his sons did Iltutmish build Sultan Ghari, the first Indo-Islamic tomb?
37.x: Sultan Ghari (1231) was built by Iltutmish for his son Nasiruddin Mahmud.

37.s: Whose tomb is the first octagonal tomb in India?
37.x: Khan-i-Jahan Tilangani's tomb, of Firoz Tughlaq's reign, is the first octagonal tomb.

37.s: Which is the earliest Indo-Islamic building and the first major Sultanate mosque in India?
37.x: The Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque in Delhi is the earliest Indo-Islamic building.

37.s: Which of the following monuments was built the earliest?
37.x: Sultan Garhi (1231) came before Alai Darwaza (1311), Tughlaqabad (1320s) and Rajon ki Baoli (c. 1506).

37.s: Which of the following is regarded as the earliest Shiva Linga?
37.x: The Gudimallam Shiva Linga (Andhra Pradesh) is regarded as the earliest Shiva Linga.

37.s: Which of the following features is associated with Sayyid and Lodi architecture rather than with the principal Tughlaq style?
o: False arches influenced by Syrian and Byzantine forms
Hindu-style gateways, plaster ornament and external drip-stones
37.x: Sayyid and Lodi builders reintroduced Hindu-style gates or façades, plaster ornament and external drip-stones.
37.tq: Identify the feature belonging to the neighbouring dynasties rather than the Tughlaq architectural vocabulary.
xs: **Hindu-style gateways, plaster ornament and external drip-stones** belong to the **Sayyid and Lodi** builders — option **(4)**.
Massive plain fort-like buildings, **battered walls**, pointed domes and **false arches** (Syrian/Byzantine) are **Tughlaq** features.
xa: Tughlaq style arose from the **Mongol threat** and finances — the "**crisis period of architecture**".
Lodi (also Sayyid) features: **octagonal tombs** and **double dome**.
Lodi Garden tombs date to the **15th-early 16th c.**

37.s: Which of the following statements regarding double domes is correct?
o: The Tughlaqs used double domes exclusively in fort gateways.
The Lodis pioneered the use of double domes on tombs, while Mughal architecture associated its first full double dome with Humayun’s Tomb.
Double domes were first introduced by the Sharqis at Atala Masjid.
Humayun’s Tomb was the first monument in India to use any form of double dome.
37.x: The Lodis pioneered double domes on tombs, while Humayun’s Tomb is credited in Mughal architectural history with the first full double dome.
37.tq: Separate the Lodi innovation from the Mughal claim concerning the first full double dome.
xs: The **Lodis pioneered** the double dome on tombs, while **Humayun's Tomb** has the first full double dome in **Mughal** architecture — option **(2)**.
So option (4) is wrong: Humayun's Tomb was not the first use of any double dome in India.
The **Tughlaqs** are known for battered walls, and the **Sharqi** Atala Masjid for its **propylon** — not double domes.
xa: Lodi examples: **Sikandar Lodi's tomb**, **Bara Gumbad**, **Shisha Gumbad** (Lodi Garden).
Lodi (and Sayyid) tombs were typically **octagonal**.
⚠ "Introduced" for Humayun's Tomb means the first **full** double dome in Mughal architecture.

37.s: For which of the following is the tomb of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq at Tughlaqabad noted?
o: A double dome on an octagonal plan
Sloping walls and a marble dome
A horseshoe arch with lotus-bud fringe
37.x: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq's tomb is noted for its sloping (battered) walls and marble dome.
xa: **Tughlaqabad** fort-city was built by **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq** — massive, rugged, built for security.
Tughlaq style is called the "**crisis period of architecture**" (Mongol threat, finances).
Qutb complex holds the **Tomb of Iltutmish**, not the Tughlaq tombs.

37.s: The horseshoe arch with a lotus-bud fringe is a feature of which architecture?
37.x: The lotus-bud horseshoe arch is Khalji; battered walls are Tughlaq, octagonal tombs and double domes Lodi, and the propylon screen Sharqi.
xa: **Sayyid and Lodi** revived Hindu elements: Hindu-style gateways, **plaster ornament**, external **drip-stones**.
Tughlaq period = "**crisis period of architecture**", due to the **Mongol threat** and finances.
Lodi examples: **Sikandar Lodi's tomb**, **Bara Gumbad**, **Shisha Gumbad** (Lodi Garden).

37.s: The domes and false arches of Tughlaq architecture show the influence of which styles?
37.x: Tughlaq domes and false arches show Syrian and Byzantine influence.
xa: The Tughlaq period is called the "**crisis period of architecture**".
Examples: **Tughlaqabad** fort-city and **Ghiyasuddin's tomb** (battered walls, **marble dome**).
First **octagonal** tomb (Khan-i-Jahan Tilangani's) also dates from the **Tughlaq** period.

37.s: Sloping (battered) walls are characteristic of which dynasty's architecture?
37.x: Tughlaq buildings are plain and fort-like with sloping (battered) walls.

37.s: What is ‘Adhai Din ka Zhonpda’?
37.x: 5. Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque and Arhai Din Ka Jhonpra are situated respectively at : (a) Delhi and Ajmer (b) Delhi and Lahore (c) Ajmer and Delhi (d) Lahore and Ajmer Jharkhand P.C.S. The topmost storey was damaged by lightning, which was rebuilt by Firuz Shah Tughluq. Firuz Shah Tughluq rebuilt the fourth floor of Qutub Minar and built the fifth floor. The Qutub Minar was completed by : (a) Iltutmish (b) Qutb-ud-din Aibak (c) Ulugh Khan (d) Raziya Sultana (e) None of the above/More than one of the above 67th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2022 Ans. (a)

37.s: The Lal Darwaza Mosque is an example of which architectural style?
37.x: Lal Darwaza is a Sharqi mosque; Moth ki Masjid is Lodi.
n: The Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque was the first major mosque of the Delhi Sultanate. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #74 · pp 152-153]
The Adhai Din Ka Jhopra is an early Sultanate mosque. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #74 · pp 152-153]
The Moth Ki Masjid represents Lodi architecture. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #74 · pp 152-153]
The Lal Darwaza Mosque represents Sharqi architecture. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #74 · pp 152-153]
xa: ⚠ Pair asked: Quwwat-ul-Islam and Adhai Din ka Jhonpra = **Delhi and Ajmer**.
Jaunpur (**Sharqi**) style: massive **propylon** screen before the prayer hall, no minarets.
**Lodis** pioneered the **double dome** on tombs.

37.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Red Palace — tomb of Alauddin Khalji
Sultan Garhi — tomb of Nasiruddin Mahmud
Jamat Khana Masjid — tomb of Iltutmish
Firoz Shah Kotla — fortress of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq
37.x: Sultan Garhi was built by Iltutmish as the tomb of his son Nasiruddin Mahmud. The Red Palace (Kushk-i-Lal) was Balban's palace, the Jamat Khana Masjid was built by Khizr Khan, son of Alauddin Khalji, and Firoz Shah Kotla was Firoz Tughlaq's citadel of Firozabad, so the other pairs are wrong.
37.tq: Use the monument’s function to reject builder or identity substitutions.

37.s: Who dug the tank at Hauz Khas, known as Hauz-i-Alai?
37.x: Alauddin Khalji excavated the Hauz-i-Alai; Firoz Shah Tughlaq later added the madrasa and tomb.
xa: Alauddin's other works: **Alai Darwaza** (**1311**), **Siri fort**, **Hazar Situm**, **Jamat Khana Masjid**.
Firoz Tughlaq also built **Firoz Shah Kotla** (Firozabad) with the **Topra Ashokan pillar**.

37.s: Where are the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque and the Adhai Din ka Jhonpra, both built by Qutbuddin Aibak, located respectively?
37.x: Quwwat-ul-Islam stands in the Qutb complex at Delhi and Adhai Din ka Jhonpra at Ajmer; both were built by Aibak. Option A reverses them; Lahore and Badaun are not the sites of these mosques.
37.tq: Quwwat = Qutb complex Delhi; Jhonpra = Ajmer.
xs: **Quwwat-ul-Islam** is at **Delhi** and **Adhai Din ka Jhonpra** at **Ajmer** — option **(2) Delhi and Ajmer**.
Option (1) reverses the two; both were built by **Qutbuddin Aibak**.
xa: Quwwat-ul-Islam reused **temple pillars** and stands in the **Qutb complex** (APPSC 2024).
Adhai Din ka Jhonpra is the "mosque at Ajmer" of the imperial style (JPSC 2021).
The **Iron Pillar** (Gupta era) stands in the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque court.

37.s: Who built the Adhai Din ka Jhonpra at Ajmer?
37.x: Adhai Din ka Jhonpra at Ajmer was built by Qutbuddin Aibak, not Iltutmish.

37.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Hazar Sutun was constructed by Sher Shah Suri.
Hauz-e-Alai was constructed by Alauddin Khalji.
Alai Darwaza was constructed by Alauddin Khalji.
37.x: Option B is incorrect: the Hazar Sutun (Hall of a Thousand Pillars) at Siri was built by Alauddin Khalji, not Sher Shah Suri. Iltutmish built the Hauz-i-Shamsi, and Alauddin built the Hauz-i-Alai and Alai Darwaza.
37.tq: Check the builder in each statement.
n: Hauz-e-Shamsi was built by Iltutmish. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 146-147]
Alai Darwaza was built by Alauddin Khalji. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 146-147]
Hazar Sutun was built by Alauddin Khalji. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 146-147]
Hauz-e-Alai was built by Alauddin Khalji. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 146-147]
xs: The incorrect statement is **"Hazar Sutun was constructed by Sher Shah Suri"** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Hazar Sutun** was built by **Alauddin Khalji**, along with **Alai Darwaza** (**1311**), **Hauz-e-Alai** and **Siri** fort.
**Hauz-e-Shamsi** was built by **Iltutmish** — true.
xa: **Sher Shah Suri** built the **Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque** at **Purana Qila** (**1541**).
**Balban** built the **Red Palace (Kushk-i-Lal)** and his tomb.
**Iltutmish** built **Sultan Ghari**, tomb of his son **Nasiruddin Mahmud**.

37.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
37.x: Tughlaqabad was built by Ghiyasuddin Tughluq. The Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque is Sher Shah Suri's, the Moth Masjid dates from Sikandar Lodi's reign and the Kirti Stambha is Rana Kumbha's.
n: Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque was built by Sher Shah Suri. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 146-147]
Moth Masjid was built during the reign of Sikandar Lodi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 146-147]
Tughluqabad was built by Ghiyasuddin Tughluq. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 146-147]
Kirti Stambha was built by Rana Kumbha. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 146-147]
xa: Qila-e-Kuhna is at **Purana Qila**, Delhi, built in **1541**.
**Tughlaqabad** was massive and rugged, built for security.
**Muhammad bin Tughlaq** built **Jahanpanah**.

37.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
37.x: Sher Shah Suri built the Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque. Aibak built the Adhai Din ka Jhopra, Iltutmish completed the Qutb Minar and Alauddin Khalji built the Alai Darwaza.
n: Adhai Din Ka Jhopara in Ajmer was built by Qutbuddin Aibak. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 146-147]
Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque in Delhi was built by Qutbuddin Aibak. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 146-147]
Construction of the Qutub Minar was started by Qutbuddin Aibak. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 146-147]
The Qutub Minar was completed by Iltutmish. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 146-147]
xa: ⚠ **Aibak** began the Minar (first storey), **Iltutmish** completed it, **Firoz Tughlaq** rebuilt the top.
The Qutb Minar is about **72.5 m**, **five** storeys.
"**Qutb Minar and its Monuments**" = UNESCO site, inscribed **1993**.

37.s: Who built the city of Jahanpanah?
37.x: Jahanpanah and a fortress at Allahabad are associated with Muhammad bin Tughlaq; Siri Fort is Alauddin's and Firoz Shah Kotla is Firoz's.
xa: **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq** built the **Tughlaqabad** fort-city — massive, rugged, built for security.
Tughlaq style: **sloping (battered) walls**, pointed domes, false arches.

37.s: Who founded Siri, one of the cities of Delhi?
37.x: Siri was founded by Alauddin Khalji; Tughlaqabad by Ghiyasuddin and Jahanpanah by Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

37.s: Which of the following pairs (city of Delhi – founder) is correctly matched?
37.x: Firozabad (Kotla) was founded by Firoz Tughlaq; Siri was Alauddin's, Tughlaqabad Ghiyasuddin's and Jahanpanah Muhammad bin Tughlaq's.

37.s: Who built the Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque (1541) in the Purana Qila, Delhi?
37.x: Sher Shah Suri built the Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque in 1541.

37.s: Who built the Jamat Khana Masjid at the Nizamuddin dargah?
37.x: The Jamat Khana Masjid was built by Khizr Khan, son of Alauddin Khalji.

37.s: Which of the following was built after Tughlaqabad Fort but before Fatehpur Sikri?
37.x: The Lodi Garden tombs (1451–1526) come between Tughlaqabad Fort (1320s) and Fatehpur Sikri (1570s).

37.s: Who built the Hazar Sutun palace at Siri?
37.x: Hazar Sutun, like the Alai Darwaza and Hauz-i-Alai, was built by Alauddin Khalji, not Sher Shah.

37.s: Who built the Red Palace (Kushk-i-Lal) at Mehrauli?
37.x: Balban built the Red Palace (Kushk-i-Lal) and his own tomb at Mehrauli.

37.s: Who added a madrasa and his own tomb at Hauz Khas, on the tank of Alauddin Khalji?
37.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq built a madrasa and his tomb at Hauz Khas beside Alauddin's tank.

37.s: In which citadel of Delhi stands the Ashokan pillar brought from Topra?
37.x: Firoz Shah Kotla, the citadel of Firozabad, holds the Topra Ashokan pillar.

37.s: During whose reign was the Moth ki Masjid in Delhi built?
37.x: The Moth ki Masjid was built in Sikandar Lodi's reign, in the Lodi style.

37.s: Who built the Kirti Stambha at Chittor?
37.x: The Kirti Stambha at Chittor is credited to Rana Kumbha of Mewar.

37.s: Which of the following is part of the 'Qutb Minar and its Monuments, Delhi' World Heritage Site?
37.x: The site includes the Qutb Minar, Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque, Alai Darwaza, Iron Pillar, Iltutmish's tomb, Alauddin's tomb and madrasa, and Imam Zamin's tomb; Tughlaqabad Fort is separate.
xa: The site was inscribed by UNESCO in **1993**.
**Iron Pillar**: Gupta era (king "Chandra" = **Chandragupta II**), famous for resisting rust.

37.s: The Iron Pillar standing in the courtyard of the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque belongs broadly to which period?
37.x: The Iron Pillar is a Gupta-era pillar. Its king Chandra is generally identified with Chandragupta II, and it is famous for its resistance to rust.
37.tq: Identify the period from the associated ruler and distinctive material feature.
xs: The **Iron Pillar** belongs to the **Gupta period** (Gupta-era) — option **(3)**.
Its king "**Chandra**" is identified with **Chandragupta II**.
xa: It is famous for **resisting rust**.
It stands in the **Quwwat-ul-Islam** mosque court, part of the **UNESCO** Qutb site (**1993**).
⚠ The **Topra Ashokan pillar** is a different pillar, at **Firoz Shah Kotla**.

37.s: How many tapering storeys does the Qutb Minar have?
37.x: The Qutb Minar has five tapering storeys, is about 72.5 metres high and bears bands of Quranic calligraphy.
xa: ⚠ Trap: "Qutb Minar is 180 ft high" is **false** (CGPSC 2023) — actually about **238 ft**.
Some notes give **73 m**.
Dedicated to Sufi saint **Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki**.

37.s: Why does the present Qutb Minar have five storeys although its upper portion was altered?
o: Iltutmish added two storeys after completing the entire monument.
Firoz Shah Tughlaq replaced the lightning-damaged top storey with two storeys.
Alauddin Khalji added two marble storeys to the original tower.
Sikandar Lodi added two storeys after rebuilding the monument.
37.x: Lightning damaged the upper portion of the Qutb Minar. Firoz Shah Tughlaq replaced the damaged top storey with two storeys made of marble and sandstone.
37.tq: Follow the cause-and-repair sequence rather than associating every addition with the original builder.
xs: **Firoz Shah Tughlaq** replaced the **lightning-damaged top storey** with **two storeys** — option **(2)**; hence **five storeys** today.
The new storeys were in **marble and sandstone**.
**Iltutmish** built storeys 2nd-4th and completed it; **Sikandar Lodi** only **repaired** it.
xa: ⚠ **Aibak** began (first storey) – **Iltutmish** completed – **Firoz Tughlaq** rebuilt the top.
Height about **72.5 m** (some notes **73 m**).

37.s: In which year was 'Qutb Minar and its Monuments, Delhi' declared a World Heritage Site?
37.x: The Qutb complex became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993.

37.s: Which of the following is NOT part of the Qutb Minar complex World Heritage Site?
37.x: Tughlaqabad Fort is not part of the Qutb WHS; Alai Darwaza, the Iron Pillar and Imam Zamin's tomb are.

37.s: Which Sultan began the Qutb Minar but built only its first storey?
37.x: Aibak began the minar and built the first storey; Iltutmish completed it.

37.s: Who built the second to fourth storeys of the Qutb Minar?
37.x: Iltutmish completed the second to fourth storeys; Firoz Tughlaq later rebuilt the top.

37.s:
Consider the following statements about the Qutb Minar:

37.x: Sikandar Lodi, like Firoz Tughlaq, repaired the minar; it is about 238 ft (72.5 m) high, not 180 ft.

37.s: With whom is the king 'Chandra' of the Iron Pillar in the Qutb complex identified?
37.x: The Gupta-period Iron Pillar's 'Chandra' is Chandragupta II.

37.s: What is the approximate height of the Qutb Minar?
37.x: The Qutb Minar is about 72.5 m (238 ft) high; the 180 ft figure is a trap.

37.s: After which Sufi saint is the Qutb Minar commonly believed to be named?
37.x: The Qutb Minar is commonly believed to be named after Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki (the point is debated).

37.s: Which one of the following monuments has a dome which is said to be one of the largest in the world?
37.x: The Gol Gumbaz in Bijapur (Vijayapura), Karnataka, is the 17 th-century mausoleum of Sultan Mohammad Adil Shah, renowned for its massive, unsupported dome—the second-largest in the world after St. Peter's Basilica.

37.s: Which of the following rulers got the Jantar Mahal of Mandu constructed?
37.x: Gujari Mahal was constructed by Raja Man Singh Tomar between 1486-1516 A.D. It is a unique piece of architecture.

37.s: Which of the following sets consists entirely of monuments associated with Bengal architecture?
o: Mahmud Gawan Madrasa, Bidar Fort and Ashtur tombs
Atala Masjid, Chand Minar and Gol Gumbaz
Charminar, Adina Mosque and Jami Masjid of Mandu
Eklakhi tomb, Dakhil Darwaza and Chota Sona Masjid
37.x: The Eklakhi tomb, Dakhil Darwaza and Chota Sona Masjid are all Bengal monuments. Option A is Bahmani (Bidar), B mixes Jaunpur, Daulatabad and Bijapur, and C mixes Hyderabad, Bengal and Mandu (Malwa).

xs: **Eklakhi tomb, Dakhil Darwaza and Chota Sona Masjid** are all **Bengal** monuments — option **(4)**.

xa: Bengal style: **brick** building, **curved roofs**.
**Adina Mosque** and the **Pandua** mosques are the earliest Bengal examples.

37.s: Who built the Chand Minar at Daulatabad in 1435?
o: Alauddin Ahmad Shah of the Bahmani dynasty
37.x: The Chand Minar at Daulatabad was built in 1435 by the Bahmani Sultan Alauddin Ahmad Shah.
37.tq: Match the monument with its correct builder and date while rejecting nearby Sultanate rulers.

94.x: Option (c) is correct: Harihara I, along with his brother Bukka, founded the Vijayanagara Empire in 1336 CE. He established a new city on the south bank of the Tungabhadra River (a tributary of the Krishna River) and named it Vijayanagara. The decline of the Hoysala kingdom enabled Harihara and Bukka to expand their newly founded kingdom. By c. 1346 CE, they brought the whole of the Hoysala kingdom under their control. Bukka succeeded his brother in c.1356 and ruled till 1377 CE. During his reign, the Sultanate of Madurai was eliminated. Option (a) is incorrect: Amoghavarsha I (c.814−878 CE) was one of the most famous of the Rashtrakutas, who built a new capital city, that of Manyakheta (modern Malkhed). He was a patron of literature and was an accomplished scholar in Kannada and Sanskrit himself. He wrote the Kavirajamarga, the earliest Kannada work on poetics, and the Prashnottara Ratnamalika in Sanskrit, which is considered a work of high merit and was later translated into Tibetan. Because of his religious temperament, his interest in the arts and literature and his peace-loving nature, he is often compared to emperor Ashoka and called "Ashoka of the South", and is also compared to Gupta king Vikramaditya in giving patronage to men of letters. Option (b) is incorrect: The Hoysalas ruled over parts of the present Karnataka and most of the Tamil region. The first independent ruler of the kingdom was Ballala II (1173-1220). 94.s: The kingdom of Vijayanagara was founded by-
94.x: The Vijayanagara empire was founded by Harihara and Bukka in 1336. This dynasty is known as Sangama Dynasty after their father’s name. Harihara and Bukka were the feudatories of the Kakatiyas of Warangal. After the fall of Warangal at the hands of Delhi Sultan, they shifted to Kampili and became ministers. Muhammad Tughluq invaded Kampili and arrested Harihara and Bukka. Both were forced to convert to Islam. Later, both were sent to the south to suppress a rebellion. They could not succeed, but under the influence of Saint Vidyaranya, they again reverted to Hinduism to establish the Vijayanagara Dynasty. They were inspired by their spiritual teacher Vidyaranya and Sayan, a noted commentator of Vedas. Four Dynasties ruled under this empire. (i) Sangama dynasty (1336-1485 A.D.). (ii) Saluva dynasty (1485-1505 A.D.), (iii) Tuluva dynasty (1505-1570 A.D.) and (vi) Aravidu dynasty (1570-1672 A.D.). These dynasties ruled over three hundred years. The capitals of Vijayanagara were Anegundi, Vijayanagara, Penukonda and Chandragiri respectively.

94.s: Who was the founder of the Tuluva Dynasty?
94.x:
The Tuluva Dynasty, the third ruling dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire, was founded by Veera Narasimha Raya in 1505 CE after the decline of the Saluva dynasty. Although Veera Narasimha founded the dynasty, it reached its greatest height under his younger brother Sri Krishnadevaraya (1509–1529 CE). During Krishnadevaraya's reign, the empire attained its political, military, economic and cultural zenith. The Tuluva rulers encouraged literature, temple construction, irrigation and foreign trade. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).
Exam Note:
• Founder – Veera Narasimha
• Greatest ruler – Sri Krishnadevaraya

94.s: Who among the following rulers of Vijayanagara Empire constructed a large dam across Tungabhadra River and canalcum-aqueduct several a kilometres long from the river to the capital city?
94.x: Deva Raya I (c. 1406–1422 CE) was a prominent ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire known for his contributions to irrigation, military organisation, and cultural patronage. He commissioned a massive dam across the Tungabhadra River along with a canal-cum-aqueduct system to supply water to the capital, and also constructed another dam on the Haridra River to support agriculture. The celebrated Hazara Rama Temple, a fine example of Deccan architecture, was built during his reign. His court was visited by travellers such as Nicolo Conti, who left valuable accounts of the empire. Deva Raya I strengthened the Vijayanagara army by improving cavalry forces, employing Turkic archers, and importing quality horses from Arabia and Persia. He was also a patron of Kannada literature and architecture, with the noted Jain poet Madhura associated with his court, a tradition that continued from his father Harihara II's time. Additional Information: The Vijayanagar kingdom constituted four dynasties — Sangama (c.1336–1485 CE), Saluva (c.1485–1503 CE), Tuluva (c.1503–1570 CE) and Aravidu (till the end of the 17 th century). Harihara and Bukka (c.1336–1377 CE) were founders of the Sangama dynasty of the Vijayanagar kingdom. Mallikarjuna, Vira Vijaya, and Virupaksha were rulers of the Sangama Dynasty, but historical records are unclear about their exact timelines, and their rule saw no significant accomplishments.

94.s: Which Vijayanagara ruler reconciled the conflict between Jains and Vaishnavas?
94.x:
Bukkaraya I, one of the founders of the Vijayanagara Empire, followed a policy of religious tolerance. When disputes arose between the Jain and Vaishnava communities, he intervened and restored harmony by granting equal protection to both religions. His policy strengthened communal peace and reflected the secular outlook of the Vijayanagara rulers, who patronized Shaivism, Vaishnavism, Jainism and other faiths. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).

• Bukkaraya I → Reconciled Jains and Vaishnavas

Allasani Peddana, honoured as the Andhra Kavita Pitamaha, was the foremost among the Ashtadiggajas in the court of Sri Krishnadevaraya. His masterpiece, Manu Charitramu (Svarochisha Manu Sambhavam), is regarded as one of the greatest works of Telugu literature. The work narrates the story of Svarochisha Manu, blending mythology with poetic imagination and philosophical thought. Because of his literary excellence, Krishnadevaraya honoured Allasani Peddana with exceptional respect, and he came to be known as the greatest poet of the Vijayanagara period. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).

95.x: The governance of Krishnadeva Raya is known as the golden age of Telugu literature. The ‘Ashtadiggajas’ were the eight great poets and scholars of Telugu in the Court of Vijayanagara. Telugu literature reached its peak during the reign of Krishnadeva Raya. He assumed the title ‘Andhra Bhoja’. ‘Peddana’ was ranked as the foremost of the 'Ashtadiggaja'. He had mastery over two languages, Telugu and Sanskrit. Krishnadeva Raya was an accomplished poet and writer. He authored ‘Amuktamalyada,’ which is considered as one of the five top Telugu epics. Krishnadeva Raya had a great interest in art and construction work. He is credited with the construction of Nagalpuram city. The Portuguese traveller Domingo Paes visited Vijayanagara during his reign. Babur mentioned Krishnadeva Raya as the most powerful of all the rulers of India in his autobiography.

Which Vijayanagara ruler patronized the Ashtadiggajas?

Sri Krishnadevaraya (1509–1529 CE) was the greatest ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire and is celebrated as one of the greatest patrons of Telugu literature. His royal court was adorned by the Ashtadiggajas (Eight Great Telugu Poets), who produced some of the finest literary works in Telugu. Among them were Allasani Peddana, Nandi Timmana, Dhurjati, Tenali Ramakrishna, Pingali Surana, Ayyalaraju Ramabhadrudu, Madayyagari Mallana and Ramarajabhushanudu. Krishnadevaraya himself was a distinguished scholar and authored the famous Telugu work Amuktamalyada. Hence, the correct answer is Option (3).

40.x: Akbar was the first among the monarchs of medieval India to raise the policy of religious tolerance to the pinnacle of secularism. The socio-political condition of the country was such that Akbar thought it was advisable to adopt independent views in religious matters. The non-Muslims constituted the majority of his Indian subjects. Without winning their confidence and active support, Akbar could not hope to establish and consolidate the Mughal rule in India. Religion had played the role of a divisive force in Indian society ever since the advent of Islam which most of its people had refused to embrace. Akbar fully understood the centrifugal tendencies of the complex Indian sociopolitical order and made a serious attempt to eliminate these by separating religion from politics. To win the goodwill of Hindus, he abolished the pilgrimage tax and Jizya. Freedom of worship, matrimonial alliances with Hindus, high civil and military positions to Hindus, translation of Hindu scriptures, establishment of Ibadatkhana, issue of infallibility decree, freedom to construct temples, land grants, considerations of Hindu sentiments, reforms in Hindu society were some measures adopted by Akbar to establish religious harmony but he had not forsaken Islam.

40.s: Which of the following families was the first to have a matrimonial alliance with Akbar?
40.x: The first matrimonial alliance with the Rajputs was established by Akbar with Kachhwaha Rajput. He went on a pilgrimage to the Mausoleum of Shaikh Muinuddin Chishti at Ajmer in 1562 A.D. His route laid through the Rajput state of Amber. Its ruler Raja Bihari Mal (Bharmal), with a view of safeguarding his position, offered his submission to Akbar at Sanganer and voluntarily proposed his daughter, Princess Harkhabai (Jodha) marriage with the young monarch. Akbar accepted the offer and on his return from Ajmer, married in 1562 AD. It was the first marriage of Akbar with any Rajput girl. Thus, Raja Bharmal was the first Rajput king who accepted Akbar’s supremacy of his accord. Salim (later Jahangir), heir to the throne was born of this wedlock on August 30, 1569 AD.

40.x: In c.1575 CE, Akbar constructed the Ibadat Khana (Hall of prayers) at his new capital, Fatehpur Sikri, wherein Akbar invited learned scholars from all religions, like Hinduism, Jainism, Christianity, and Zoroastrianism and used to conduct religious discussions with them. Some of the prominent scholars associated with Akbar's court included Purushottam Das, a Hindu Dastur; Maharji Rana, a Parsi scholar from Navsari; and Hira Vijaya Suri, a Jain saint from Kathiawar. Among the Christian scholars were Aquaviva and Monserrate, who were sent by the Portuguese at Akbar's request. In c.1582 CE, he promulgated a new religion called Din-i-Ilahi/Tauhidi-Ilahi (Divine Monotheism), which believes in one God and in Sulh-i-Kul/peace to all. It contained the good points of all religions, and the basics were rational. However, his new faith proved to be a failure. It fizzled out after his death. Even during his lifetime, it had only followers, including Birbal, Abul Fazl, and Abul Faizi.

40.s: Who constructed Ibadat Khana ?

Mahzarnama put an end to the predominance of the bigoted orthodox and allowed the free development of the generous spirit which Akbar wished to encourage. 40.tq: Match the criticism with the correct orthodox scholars rather than with supporters or foreign visitors.
xs: Orthodox criticism of Akbar's religious innovations came from **Badauni** and the Naqshbandi **Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Sirhindi** (**Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani**) attacked Akbar's **Sulh-i-kul** and **Din-i-Ilahi**.
**Faizi** and **Abul Fazl** were members of Din-i-Ilahi; **Abul Fazl** was its chief exponent.
**Hiravijaya Suri** and **Jinachandra Suri** were Jain monks honoured by Akbar; **Acquaviva** and **Jerome Xavier** led Jesuit missions from Goa.
xa: **Naqshbandi** order: founded by **Baha-ud-din Naqshband**; came to India with **Babur**; stressed strict **Sharia**.
Sirhindi propounded **Wahdat-ul-Shuhud** (Unity of Appearance) against **Wahdat-ul-Wujud**.
**Badauni** wrote the **Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh**.
Din-i-Ilahi (**1582**) had about **18** members; **Birbal** was the only Hindu disciple.

40.s: Dara Shikoh was a follower of which Sufi order?
40.x: Dara Shikoh followed the Qadiri order, associated with Abdul Qadir Jilani.
xa: The Naqshbandi order came to India with **Babur** and stressed strict **Sharia**.
**Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi** (**Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani**), a Naqshbandi, criticised **Sulh-i-kul** and **Din-i-Ilahi**.
Later Naqshbandi scholars: **Shah Waliullah** and **Shah Abdul Aziz**.

40.s: Shahabuddin was associated with which Sufi order?
40.x: Shahabuddin belonged to the Suhrawardi order, which Bahauddin Zakariya brought to Multan. The Chishti, Naqshbandi and Qadiri orders were led by other saints.
40.tq: Link the saint to his Sufi order.
n: Muinuddin Chishti belonged to the Chishti order. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Ahmad Sirhindi belonged to the Naqshbandi order. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Dara Shukoh belonged to the Qadiri order. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Shahabuddin belonged to the Suhrawardi order. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Shahabuddin is associated with Suhrawardiya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
xs: **Shahabuddin** belonged to the **Suhrawardi order** (Suhrawardiya) — option **(2)**.
**Ahmad Sirhindi** belonged to the **Naqshbandi** order.
**Dara Shukoh** belonged to the **Qadiri** order.
xa: Naqshbandi founder: **Baha-ud-din Naqshband**; came to India with **Babur**; strict **Sharia**.
Qadiri founder: **Abdul Qadir Jilani**; stood for **Wahdat-ul-Wujud**.
Sirhindi (**Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani**) propounded **Wahdat-ul-Shuhud** and attacked **Din-i-Ilahi**.

40.s: Din-i-Ilahi had about how many members?
40.x: Din-i-Ilahi was a small voluntary circle of about 18 members.

40.s: Who is regarded as the chief exponent ('prophet') of Din-i-Ilahi?
40.x: Abul Fazl was its chief exponent; Badauni and Ahmad Sirhindi were its orthodox critics.

40.s: Who founded the Naqshbandi Sufi order?
40.x: The Naqshbandi order was founded by Baha-ud-din Naqshband in the 14th century and came to India with Babur.

40.s: To which Sufi order did Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi, known as Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani, belong?
40.x: Ahmad Sirhindi was a Naqshbandi, the most orthodox order, and criticised Akbar's religious ideas.

40.s: Who among the following called Din-i-Ilahi a religion in his Dabistan-i-Mazahib?
40.x: Mohsin Fani, a contemporary of Jahangir, called it a religion in the Dabistan-i-Mazahib.

40.s: Who founded the Qadiri Sufi order?
40.x: The Qadiri order was founded by Abdul Qadir Jilani; Dara Shikoh followed it.

40.s: Who brought the Suhrawardi Sufi order to Multan?
40.x: The Suhrawardi order of Shahabuddin was brought to Multan by Bahauddin Zakariya.

40.s: What among the following is/are true about the priests who were sent to Akbar's court to resolve his curiosities toward Christianity in 1595 by Goa Church Authorities? (i) This was the third mission of Goa Church Authorities which was sent to Akbar's court. (ii) This session met Akbar in Lahore. (iii)Antonio Monserrate was included in this mission.
40.x: The third Jesuit mission reached Lahore in May 1595 under Jerome Xavier, Pinheiro and Bento de Goes, and Monserrate belonged to the first mission of 1580.

40.s: Who among the following was conferred with the title of 'Jagat Guru' by Akbar?
40.x: Hari Vijay Suri was a Jain monk who stayed for a few years in the court of Akbar and was honoured with the title of Jagadguru. Emperor Akbar invited Hari Vijay Suri to explain the principles of Jainism. Akbar was so much influenced by the ideology of non-violence preached by Jain sage that he became vegetarian and prohibited slaughter of animals and birds. Another Jain scholar who resided in Mughal court was Jin Chandra Suri bestowed with the title of "Yug Pradhan" by Akbar.

40.s: Who led the first Jesuit mission to Akbar's court (1580)?
40.x: The first Jesuit mission from Goa in 1580 was led by Rudolf Acquaviva and Antonio Monserrate; Jerome Xavier led the third mission in 1595.
xa: The second mission came in **1591**.
The missions came from **Goa**.

40.s: Under whose leadership was the third Jesuit mission to Akbar's court in 1595 conducted?
40.x: The third Jesuit mission, sent in 1595, was under Jerome Xavier.
40.tq: Distinguish the leader of the later mission from those of the first mission.
xs: The **third** Jesuit mission (**1595**) was led by **Jerome Xavier** (CGPSC **2022**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Rudolf Acquaviva** and **Antonio Monserrate** led the **first** (**1580**).
**Dastur Meherji Rana** was a **Parsi** leader.
xa: The second mission came in **1591**.
The Ibadat Khana was opened to **Christians** among others.

40.s: With the growth of which city is Akbar's grant of land to Guru Ram Das associated?
40.x: Land granted to Guru Ram Das became associated with the growth of Amritsar.
40.tq: Link the religious leader with the place connected to the grant.
xs: Akbar's land grant to **Guru Ram Das** is where **Amritsar** grew — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Fatehpur Sikri** housed the **Ibadat Khana**.
xa: **Guru Arjan Dev** built the **Golden Temple (Harmandir)** at Amritsar.
Guru Arjan Dev was **executed by Jahangir (1606)**.
Akbar also gave land to Parsi **Dastur Meherji Rana**.

40.s: On which Jain scholar did Akbar confer the title 'Yuga Pradhan'?
40.x: Jinachandra Suri was called Yuga Pradhan; Hiravijaya Suri received the title Jagat Guru.

40.s: Which Parsi priest received a land grant from Akbar?
40.x: Dastur Meherji Rana, a Parsi, received a land grant; Xavier and Acquaviva were Jesuits.

40.s: In which year did the second Jesuit mission from Goa reach Akbar's court?
40.x: The Jesuit missions came in 1580, 1591 and 1595; 1591 was the second.

40.s: Whose name called Ata Ali Khan?
40.x: "Iqta" was allotted by Delhi Sultans, Jagir was allotted by Mughal rulers, Amaram land grant was made by Vijayanagara rulers and Mokasa land was granted by Maratha rulers.

40.s: The original name of Tansen was :
40.x: The original name of Tansen was Ramtanu Pandey. He was a prominent Hindustani classical music composer and musician. He was among the Navaratnas (nine jewels) at the court of the Mughal Emperor Akbar. Akbar gave him the title ‘Miyan.’ His contribution to the world of music is priceless and is still worshipped by leading singers and composers of the world. Akbar gave the title ‘Kanthabharanvanivilas’ to Tansen.

40.s: Abul Fazl’s death was caused by –
40.x: Behind Abul Fazl’s death was Prince Salim. When Prince Salim started behaving as independent King at Allahabad (Prayagraj) and became rebellious, Akbar called Abul Fazal from Deccan in 1602 AD. Vir Singh Bundela assassinated Abul Fazl in a plot contrived by Mughal prince while he was returning from Deccan.

40.s: The killer of Abul Fazl was rewarded by :
40.x: The coronation of Jahangir took place in November, 1605 AD. A week after the death of Akbar he assumed the title of ‘Nuruddin Muhammad Jahangir Badshah Ghazi.’ He provided high designations to his associates in his court in which the murderer of Abul Fazl, Raja Vir Singh Bundela was also rewarded. Jahangir started his reign with liberalism forwarding the customs and traditions of his father Akbar and issued the orders which demonstrated concern for the welfare of the people.

40.s: The translation of the Mahabharat into Persian in the time of Akbar was carried out under the supervision of :
40.x: Akbar established Translation Department under the supervision of his poet laureate Abul Fazl. The translation of the Mahabharat into Persian at the time of Akbar was carried out under the direction of Faizi by the concerted effort of Naqib Khan, Badauni, Faizi etc.

40.s: Who among the following kings had given patronage to Tansen before Akbar?
The medieval Indian writer who refers to the discovery of America is
40.x: Abul Fazl was aware of the discovery of America by Europeans: he gives the Persian term alam nau for the "New World". But this knowledge does not appear to have become a standard part of geography teaching in India.

40.s: The medieval Indian writer who refers to the discovery of America is :
40.x: Abul Fazl was a writer of medieval period who refers to the discovery of America.

40.s: Which state did Tansen's early patron, Raja Ramchandra Singh, rule?
40.x: Tansen was first patronised by Raja Ramchandra Singh of Rewa before joining Akbar's court as a Navaratna.
n: Raja Ramchandra Singh of Rewa was an early patron of Tansen. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #47 · pp 115-116]
Tansen was a Navaratna in Akbar’s court. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #47 · pp 115-116]
Swami Haridas was associated with Dhrupad. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #47 · pp 115-116]
Vilas Khan was a main singer in Jahangir’s court. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #47 · pp 115-116]
xa: Tansen (**Ramtanu Pandey**) is credited with **Miyan ki Malhar** and **Miyan ki Todi**.
**Hari Vijay Suri**, a Jain monk, was a **Jagadguru**; **Jin Chandra Suri** a **Yug Pradhan**.
**Faizi** supervised Akbar's **translation department**.

40.s: Which statement regarding Raja Todar Mal is correct?
o: He served Aurangzeb and had earlier served Murshid Quli Khan.
He served only the Qutb Shahis and introduced the Pargana system.
He was a provincial Qazi who designed the Mansabdari system.
He served Akbar and had earlier served Sher Shah.
40.x: Todar Mal was Akbar's revenue minister and had earlier served Sher Shah. His system was modelled on Sher Shah's survey-based arrangements.
40.tq: Use the predecessor-service link to distinguish Todar Mal from other administrative figures.
xs: **Todar Mal** served **Akbar** and had earlier served **Sher Shah** — so option **(4)** is correct.
His Zabti was modelled on **Sher Shah's survey-based system**.
xa: He designed the **Zabti / Bandobast (dahsala)** in **1580**.
He is listed among the prominent Rajputs with **Man Singh** and **Birbal**.
He died in **1589**.

40.s: Who was the only Hindu member of Din-i-Ilahi?
40.x: Birbal was the only Hindu member of Din-i-Ilahi. The circle of members was small, numbering about 18 according to the cited account.
40.tq: Distinguish the sole Hindu member from other prominent Hindu officials at Akbar's court.
xs: **Birbal** was the **only Hindu** disciple of Din-i-Ilahi — so option **(3)** is correct.
The circle was small — about **18** members.
xa: Other members: **Abul Fazl, Faizi and Shaikh Mubarak**.
Birbal (Mahesh Das) was killed in **1586** fighting the **Yusufzai**.
**Man Singh** and **Todar Mal** are not listed as members.

40.s: Who designed the Zabti or Dahsala system?
40.x: Raja Todar Mal designed the Zabti, also called Bandobast or Dahsala, revenue system.
xs: **Raja Todar Mal** designed the **Zabti / Bandobast / Dahsala** system — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Abul Fazl** wrote the **Akbarnama**; **Man Singh** was a general; **Birbal** a wit and adviser.
xa: It was modelled on **Sher Shah's** survey-based system.
Land was measured with the bamboo **Gaz-i-Ilahi** (about **82** cm).
Revenue = **one-third** of average produce of the last **10** years.

40.s: Under what name was the Mahabharata translated in Akbar's time?
40.x: The Mahabharata was rendered as the Razmnama; the Atharvaveda was also translated.
xa: **Faizi** (Abul Fazl's brother) made the Persian **Lilavati**.
**Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan** made a Persian translation of the **Baburnama**.
**Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh** — **Badauni**; **Tabaqat-i-Akbari** — **Nizamuddin Ahmad**.

40.s: Who wrote Akbarnama and was associated with Akbar as a scholar and court intellectual?
40.x: Abul Fazl, Akbar's court historian, wrote the Akbarnama and Ain-i-Akbari and rendered the Panchatantra as Ayar-i-Danish. Faizi was his brother and poet laureate.
40.tq: Link the work to its author.
n: Abul Fazl was a scholar and court intellectual. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 113-115]
Abul Fazl was associated with Akbar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 113-115]
xs: **Abul Fazl** — option **(1)**.
He wrote the **Akbarnama** and **Ain-i-Akbari** and was Akbar's **scholar and court intellectual**.
**Faizi**, his brother, was the **poet laureate**; **Nizamuddin Panipati** translated the **Yogavasistha** into Persian.
xa: Abul Fazl translated the **Panchatantra** into **Ayar-i-Danish**.
He was **murdered** in **1602** by **Bir Singh Bundela** at **Salim's** instance.
Order of deaths: **Sheikh Mubarak → Faizi → Abul Fazl → Prince Daniyal**.

40.s: Who translated the Baburnama into Persian?
40.x: Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan, son of Bairam Khan, translated the Baburnama into Persian.
xa: ⚠ Some notes wrongly credit **Tabaqat-i-Akbari** to Badauni.
Faizi was **poet laureate** and Abul Fazl's brother.
The **Razmnama** is the translation of the **Mahabharata**.

40.s: What was Akbar's translation bureau at Fatehpur Sikri called?
40.x: The Maktab Khana ('House of Translation') was Akbar's translation bureau; the Ibadat Khana was the hall of religious debate.

40.s: Around which year was Akbar's Maktab Khana set up?
40.x: The Maktab Khana was set up at Fatehpur Sikri around 1574.

40.s: Who translated the Yogavasistha into Persian under Akbar?
40.x: Nizamuddin Panipati translated the Yogavasistha; Abdur Rahim translated the Baburnama.

40.s: Which of the following about Fatehpur Sikri is NOT correct?
o: The Buland Darwaza there commemorates the conquest of Bengal.
The Ibadat Khana was built there in 1575.
The first Jesuit mission reached it in 1580.
40.x: The Buland Darwaza commemorates the Gujarat conquest (1572-73), not Bengal.

40.s: While fighting whom was Raja Birbal killed in 1586?
40.x: Birbal was killed in 1586 fighting the Yusufzai.

40.s: By whom was Abul Fazl murdered in 1602?
o: Man Singh I at Akbar's instance
Adham Khan at Bairam Khan's instance
Bir Singh Bundela at Salim's instance
40.x: Abul Fazl was murdered in 1602 by Bir Singh Bundela at the instance of Prince Salim.
40.tq: Use the wrong-person and wrong-instigator trap in a court event.
xs: **Abul Fazl** was murdered in **1602** by **Bir Singh Bundela** at **Salim's** instance — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Adham Khan** belongs to the **petticoat government**; **Hemu** died at **Panipat II**.
xa: Abul Fazl wrote the **Akbarnama** and **Ain-i-Akbari**.
He was the chief exponent of **Din-i-Ilahi**.
Order of deaths: **Sheikh Mubarak → Faizi → Abul Fazl → Prince Daniyal** (UPPSC **2024**).

40.s: Which one of Akbar's court figures, originally named Ramtanu Pandey, is associated with the ragas Miyan ki Malhar and Miyan ki Todi?
40.x: Tansen (Ramtanu Pandey) was the court musician credited with Miyan ki Malhar and Miyan ki Todi. Faizi was the poet laureate, Birbal (Mahesh Das) the wit and adviser, and Abdur Rahim a poet known for Hindi dohas.
xs: **Tansen** (Ramtanu Pandey) is linked to **Miyan ki Malhar** and **Miyan ki Todi** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Faizi** was the **poet laureate**; **Birbal** (Mahesh Das) the wit and adviser; **Abdur Rahim** a poet of Hindi **dohas**.
xa: Tansen is credited with a **gharana** tradition and linked to **Gwalior**.
**Man Singh I** led the Mughals at Haldighati.

40.s: Which conquest of Akbar does the Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri commemorate?
40.x: The Buland Darwaza marks the Gujarat conquest of 1572-73.

40.s: Who translated the Lilavati into Persian in Akbar's time?
40.x: Faizi, Akbar's poet laureate and Abul Fazl's brother, made the Persian Lilavati.

40.s: Under what name did Abul Fazl render the Panchatantra into Persian?
40.x: Abul Fazl's Persian Panchatantra is the Ayar-i-Danish.

40.s: Who was the father of Abul Fazl and Faizi?
40.x: Sheikh Mubarak, who drafted the Mahzar, was the father of Abul Fazl and Faizi.

40.s: Which title did Akbar confer on Tansen?
40.x: Akbar gave Tansen the title 'Miyan' (hence Miyan ki Malhar); the name Tansen came from an earlier Hindu patron.

40.s: What condition is described as the jagirdari crisis under Aurangzeb?
o: Too many jagirdars competing for too few jagirs, placing pressure on the peasantry
The complete abolition of jagirs by Akbar
The transfer of all jagirs to Rajput rulers
Too few mansabdars controlling an excessive number of jagirs

40.s: In Mughal revenue practice, what did 'Kankut' mean?
o: A fixed cash rate per bigha
40.x: Kankut estimated the standing crop; Batai was crop-sharing and Nasaq was based on past payments.

Relief came through **Taccavi** loans.

40.s: Under Akbar's Zabti system, how was land that had been left fallow for three to four years classified?
40.x: Chachar was land fallow for 3-4 years. Polaj was cultivated every year, Parauti was fallow for 1-2 years, and Banjar was uncultivated for 5 years or more.

o: Dahsala (Zabti) – Average produce and prices over ten years

40.s: From about which period do the dual ranks of Zat and Sawar in Akbar's mansabdari date?
40.x: Zat and Sawar dual ranks came about 1595-96; 1573-74 was the Dagh system.

40.s: Who introduced the du-aspa sih-aspa system?
40.x: Du-aspa sih-aspa was Jahangir's measure, first for Mahabat Khan; Zat-Sawar was Akbar's.

Consider the following statements about the mansabdari system:

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
40.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; du-aspa sih-aspa was introduced by Jahangir, not Akbar.

40.s: Which of the following pairs (Land assignment – Rulers) is NOT correctly matched?
40.x: Mokasa was the Maratha assignment; the Mughals used jagirs.

40.s: Which Mughal Emperor abolished the Persian Court Custom of ‘Sijda’ which was begun by Balban?
40.x: Shah Jahan was the Mughal emperor who abolished the Persian court custom of Sijda which was begun by Balban.

40.s: Which of the following Mughal Emperors introduced educational reforms?
40.x: Akbar was the Mughal emperor who introduced educational reforms in the curriculum of learning, especially at the primary level. Certain important subjects like arithmetic, logic mensuration, geometry, astronomy, physiognomy, accountancy, public administration and agriculture were included in the course of study at his command. Though he received no formal education, he patronized men of learning.

40.s: Which one of the following emperors had the highest number of Hindu Generals in the Mughal army:
40.x: The Mughal army had the largest number of Hindu Generals during the reign of Aurangzeb. There were 31.6% Hindu commanders in Aurangzeb’s court in which most of the members were Marathas. This ratio was 22.5% in Akbar’s reign and 22.4% during Shah Jahan’s reign.

40.s: Which Mughal Emperor was known as "Zinda Peer" ?
40.x: Aurangzeb was a remarkable man. Among the Mughals, he possessed extraordinary personal qualities. He maintained high moral standards and was far from vices, pleasures and extravagance. Some recommended him ‘Shahi Darvesh’ and some Muslims accepted him as "Zinda Peer".

40.s: Which of the following Mughal Emperors wrote his autobiography in Persian ?
40.x: Jahangir was an outstanding author as well as a critic. He wrote his autobiography in Persian language and named it Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri. Jahangir had recorded his merits as well as demerits in his autobiography. This memoir has been divided into three parts. The first part is the preface which was written by Muhammad Hadi after the death of Jahangir in which the early life of Jahangir is mentioned. The second part was an original piece of text narrated by Jahangir. The third part of the text was written by Muhammad Hadi. Babur wrote his autobiography ‘Tuzuk-i-Babri’’ in the Turkish language.

40.s: Which of the following statements about the Mughal emperors is correct?
o: Babur adopted the title Zinda Pir.
Shah Jahan received the title 'Shah Jahan' from Jahangir.
Aurangzeb was known as Nur-ud-din Muhammad Jahangir.

40.tq: Use swapped royal titles as the principal trap.
xs: **Shah Jahan** received the title **"Shah Jahan" from Jahangir** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Zinda Pir** was a name of **Aurangzeb**, not Babur.
**Nur-ud-din Muhammad Jahangir** was Jahangir's coronation name; **Alamgir** was Aurangzeb's title.
xa: **Babur** took the title **Padshah** and, at **Khanwa**, the title **Ghazi**.
Aurangzeb was also called **Darvesh**; he was learned in Arabic and Persian.
**Akbar** was the **unlettered** emperor; **Humayun** was learned in **astronomy** and mathematics.

40.s: Which of the following describes Jahangir's religious policy?
o: A complete break from Akbar's tolerance
Broadly continuing Akbar's tolerance, though Guru Arjan Dev was executed for political reasons
40.x: Jahangir broadly continued Akbar's tolerance; Guru Arjan Dev was executed for political reasons linked to support for the rebel prince Khusrau.
xa: **Guru Arjan Dev** was executed in **1606** for supporting rebel prince **Khusrau**.
Jahangir imprisoned **Guru Hargobind** at **Gwalior**.
Jahangir gave Prince Khurram the title **"Shah Jahan"**.

40.s: Under which emperor did the Mughal Empire reach its maximum territorial extent?
40.x: Aurangzeb's Deccan conquests of Bijapur and Golconda gave the empire its greatest extent.
n: Aurangzeb's reign marked the maximum territorial expansion of the Mughal Empire. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Aurangzeb commissioned the Fatawa-i-Alamgiri. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
xa: Aurangzeb had the **highest number of Hindu nobles** in absolute terms (UPPSC **2000** key), largely Marathas and Rajputs.

40.x: The first matrimonial alliance with the Rajputs was established by Akbar with Kachhwaha Rajput. He went on a pilgrimage to the Mausoleum of Shaikh Muinuddin Chishti at Ajmer in 1562 A.D. His route laid through the Rajput state of Amber. Its ruler Raja Bihari Mal (Bharmal), with a view of safeguarding his position, offered his submission to Akbar at Sanganer and voluntarily proposed his daughter, Princess Harkhabai (Jodha) marriage with the young monarch. Akbar accepted the offer and on his return from Ajmer, married in 1562 AD. It was the first marriage of Akbar with any Rajput girl. Thus, Raja Bharmal was the first Rajput king who accepted Akbar’s supremacy of his accord. Salim (later Jahangir), heir to the throne was born of this wedlock on August 30, 1569 AD.

43.x: During the medieval period, the Indian trading classes were large in number, widely spread throughout the country, and well organised. This system was launched in Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, Varanasi (U.P.) etc. It is also known as Istimarari Maalguzari, Bishwedari etc. The Permanent Settlement stood on the following features - It recognized the landlords as the proprietors of the land. It also recognized the rights of a hereditary successor or lawful successors of the landlords. The government believed that these landlords would remain faithful to the British. The landlords were given the right to transfer or sell their land. All the rights of the landlords depended on their payment of the fixed revenue on the fixed date at the treasury of the government. 45.s: Who among the following Mughal Emperors shifted emphasis from illustrated manuscripts to album and individual portrait?
45.x: Jahangir (c. 1605–1627 CE) presided over the zenith of Mughal painting. He patronised several distinguished artists, including Abul Hasan, Bishan Das (renowned as a master of portraiture), Madhu, Anant, Manohar, Govardhan, and Ustad Mansur, who specialised in animal painting. During his reign, the use of the halo or divine light behind the emperor's head became a prominent artistic feature. The artistic focus also shifted from illustrated manuscripts to muraqqas—albums of miniature paintings and calligraphic works. Stylistically, Jahangir favoured naturalism, incorporating elements of Persian painting while placing strong emphasis on portraiture.

His descendants and disciples are called Seniyas.

46.s: Who were the first Vaishnavite devotees in South India?
46.x:
The Alwars were the earliest Vaishnavite Bhakti saints of South India who flourished between the 6th and 9th centuries CE. They composed devotional hymns in praise of Lord Vishnu, which were later compiled into the Nalayira Divya Prabandham. Their teachings emphasized personal devotion (Bhakti) rather than rituals and played a crucial role in spreading the Bhakti Movement throughout South India. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).

46.s: Who were Nayanars?

The devotees worshipping God Vishnu were called Alvar and the devotees worshiping God Shiva were called Nayanara. They said that personal love and dedication towards God is the only way to Moksha and opposed the caste system and its rigidity.

Tyagaraja and his contemporaries, Shyam Shastri and Muthuswami Dikshitai, were regarded as a trinity of Carnatic Music. Tyagaraja composed thousands of devotional compositions, most in Telugu and praise of Lord Rama. He created several new ragas. 47.s: Who is the foremost composer of Carnatic music?
47.x:
Saint Thyagaraja (1767–1847) is regarded as one of the greatest composers of Carnatic music and is revered as a member of the Carnatic Trinity, along with Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri. He composed thousands of devotional Kritis, most of them dedicated to Lord Rama. His compositions are known for their profound devotion, musical excellence and philosophical depth, making them central to the Carnatic music tradition. Although Annamacharya composed over 32,000 Sankirtanas in praise of Lord Venkateswara and is regarded as the Padakavita Pitamaha, the title of the foremost composer of Carnatic music is associated with Saint Thyagaraja. His annual Thyagaraja Aradhana at Tiruvaiyaru continues to attract musicians from across the world. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).
Exam Note:
• Foremost Composer of Carnatic Music – Saint Thyagaraja
• Carnatic Trinity – Thyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, Syama Sastri
• Devotional Deity – Lord Rama
